📌 Our main goals are:

1️⃣ Spread awareness of member states’ culture, and traditions.

For years, Eastern European countries have gotten little coverage within university curricula. By starting this association, we aim to raise awareness of our countries’ present-day achievements, as well as historical and cultural richness, through events, discussions, and festivals.

2️⃣ Promote an academic focus on member states’ political and historical developments.

When viewing developments of our countries, little is known to the general public outside of the headline stories. We strive to share knowledge of the intricate workings of our histories and political systems through an academic lens to provide greater context and deeper understanding.

3️⃣ Maintain attention on Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

For more than four years, Ukraine has been bravely defending its right to freedom and democracy. We aim to do everything possible to support Ukrainian students and to remind our communities about the hardships Ukrainian people are facing.

Why is Ukraine even still at war? What does this conflict mean for Europe’s future? 🇺🇦🇪🇺

Join Andrey Kurkov, one of Ukraine’s most celebrated authors, for a special talk at Universiteit Leiden, The Hague Campus, on 11 December 2025, organized by Agorá and ABBA Student Association.

The current Russo-Ukrainian war has lasted for more than 10 years and it has already become the pivotal point of European history. Few can describe this reality as vividly and humanely as Andrey Kurkov, who continues to live and write in Ukraine despite the ongoing war. In this discussion, Kurkov will share his personal experiences on how the war affects not only Ukrainian society but also the broader European community – its security, its values, and its future.  Andrey Kurkov is the author of over 20 novels and 10 books for children, translated into more than 45 languages. He is also a columnist for The Guardian, Financial Times, New Statesman, The Spectator, and other media.
